title: Cajun-Style Sausage and Rice with Peppers and Celery
description: Browned pork sausage, the onion-pepper-celery trinity, tomatoes and long-grain rice, all cooked in one covered pot. One pound of sausage feeds six at under $2 a serving.
notes: Sweet Italian sausage keeps this mild enough for children; use hot sausage or more cayenne if everyone likes heat. Smoked andouille or kielbasa works too: it is already cooked, so brown the slices for 3 minutes and carry on. Check the sausage label if you need the dish gluten-free, since a few brands add fillers. A lightly crusted layer on the bottom of the pot is fine, but a burnt smell means the heat was too high, so use your lowest setting next time. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days, or freeze up to 2 months. Reheat covered with a splash of water until steaming and 165°F in the center.

ingredients.name: fresh sweet or hot italian pork sausage, casings removed
cayenne pepper, plus more to taste
long grain white rice (285 g), rinsed and drained
fire-roasted diced tomatoes (15 oz), with their juice
louisiana-style cayenne pepper hot sauce, for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and break it into bite-size crumbles with a wooden spoon. Let it sit for 2 minutes to brown, then stir and cook until well browned with no pink left, 6 to 8 minutes total; it should reach 160°F. Leave the fat in the pot.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion, bell pepper, celery and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Cook, scraping up the browned bits, until the onion is soft and translucent, 6 to 7 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, thyme, oregano and cayenne and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the rice and stir for 1 minute so every grain is coated and glossy.

Pour in the tomatoes with their juice and the broth, then add the bay leaf, the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and several grinds of pepper. Stir once, scraping the bottom of the pot, and bring to a lively boil.

Cover, turn the heat to low and cook without lifting the lid for 20 minutes. The liquid should be absorbed and the rice tender; if it is still firm, sprinkle in 2 tablespoons water, cover and cook 3 to 5 minutes more.

Turn off the heat and let the pot stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Remove the bay leaf, fluff the rice with a fork, taste for salt and cayenne, and scatter the scallions over the top. Pass hot sauce at the table.

title: Moroccan-Inspired Chicken Thighs with Chickpeas, Carrots and Lemon
description: Bone-in chicken thighs browned and braised in one pot with warm spices, carrots and two cans of chickpeas, finished with lemon and cilantro. The chickpeas stretch six thighs to feed six.
notes: Serve with warm bread to soak up the sauce, or over couscous if you have a second pot free (bread and couscous add wheat). Boneless skinless thighs work too: brown them 3 minutes per side and simmer about 15 minutes, until they reach 165°F. Butternut squash or sweet potato can replace half the carrots. Leave out the cayenne for small children and pass hot sauce at the table instead. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; the flavor improves overnight. Freeze up to 3 months, and reheat covered over medium-low heat until the chicken is 165°F.

ingredients.name: carrots (about 4), peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks
chickpeas (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
lemon, zest finely grated and juice squeezed

instructions: Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, mix 1 teaspoon of the salt with the pepper, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon and cayenne. Rub half the spice mixture over the chicken and save the rest for the sauce.

Heat the oil in a 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven over medium heat. Lay the thighs in skin side down and cook without moving them until the skin is deep golden and releases easily, 8 to 10 minutes. Turn and cook 3 minutes more, then move to a plate. Pour off all but about 2 tablespoons of fat.

Add the onion and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and cook, scraping up the browned bits, until soft and golden at the edges, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, tomato paste and the rest of the spice mixture and cook, stirring, until the paste darkens a shade, about 1 minute.
Add the carrots, chickpeas, broth, raisins if using, and the lemon zest. Bring to a simmer, then nestle the chicken back in skin side up, keeping the skin above the liquid so it stays fairly crisp.

Cover, lower the heat to medium-low and simmer gently until the carrots are tender and the thickest thigh reads 165°F near the bone, 30 to 35 minutes. Thighs grow more tender toward 175°F, so a few extra minutes does no harm.
Uncover and simmer 5 minutes to thicken the sauce slightly. Stir the lemon juice into the sauce around the chicken, taste for salt, and scatter the cilantro over the top before serving.

title: Thai-Style Coconut Chicken Soup with Lemongrass and Mushrooms
description: A tom kha-inspired soup of chicken thighs and mushrooms simmered in coconut milk and broth scented with lemongrass and ginger, balanced with lime and fish sauce. One pot, about 40 minutes.
notes: Galangal is traditional; if you can find it, use it in place of the ginger for a sharper, piney flavor. Light coconut milk makes a thinner soup. Ladling it over leftover jasmine rice turns six bowls into a more filling dinner. For a vegetarian version, use cubed extra-firm tofu instead of chicken (adds soy), vegetable broth, and gluten-free tamari in place of the fish sauce (removes fish). Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 3 days; the coconut fat firms when cold and melts back as it warms. Reheat gently, without boiling, until steaming and 165°F, and add a squeeze of fresh lime. Freezing is not recommended because the coconut milk turns grainy.

ingredients.name: lemongrass stalks, trimmed, cut into 2-inch lengths and bruised
serrano or green chile, halved lengthwise
boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed and sliced 1/4 inch thick
full-fat coconut milk (13.5 oz each), well shaken
fish sauce, plus more to taste

instructions: Put the lemongrass, ginger, garlic and chile in a 4- to 5-quart pot with the broth. Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower the heat, cover and simmer 10 minutes so the aromatics flavor the broth.
Add the chicken and mushrooms, return to a gentle simmer and cook, stirring once or twice, until the chicken is opaque all the way through and reads 165°F, 6 to 8 minutes.

Stir in the coconut milk, fish sauce, sugar and salt, plus the cherry tomatoes if using. Heat just until steaming and barely bubbling at the edges, about 4 minutes; a hard boil can make the coconut milk separate.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lime juice. Taste and adjust: the soup should be rich, tangy and gently salty, so add fish sauce for salt or lime for brightness a teaspoon at a time.
Lift out the lemongrass, ginger slices and chile with a slotted spoon, or tell everyone to eat around them. Ladle into bowls and top with the cilantro and scallions.

title: German-Style Beef and Cabbage Skillet with Potatoes and Caraway
description: One pound of ground beef, half a head of cabbage and a few potatoes cook down together in one covered pan with caraway, paprika and a splash of cider vinegar. Hearty and cheap at about $1.75 a serving for six.
equipment: 12-inch deep skillet with lid, or a 5-quart Dutch oven
notes: Ground turkey (93% lean) works in place of the beef; add 1 tablespoon oil to the pan and cook it to 165°F. Red cabbage makes a purple, slightly sweeter dish. If caraway is not a favorite, use 1 teaspoon dried thyme instead. A spoonful of sour cream on each plate is traditional and adds milk. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water until it reaches 165°F. Freezing softens the potatoes, so this is best eaten within the week.

ingredients.name: large yellow onion, halved and sliced
russet or yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
green cabbage (about half a medium head), cored and sliced 1/2 inch thick

instructions: Set a 12-inch deep skillet or 5-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the beef and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and break the meat into small pieces. Cook, stirring now and then, until browned with no pink left and it reaches 160°F, 7 to 8 minutes. Spoon off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat.
Add the onion and carrot and cook until the onion softens and turns golden at the edges, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, caraway seeds and paprika and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add the potatoes, broth and 1/2 teaspoon salt, scrape up the browned bits, and bring to a simmer. Cover, lower the heat to medium-low and cook 8 minutes, until the potatoes are starting to soften at the edges.

Pile the cabbage on top, sprinkle with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, cover and cook 5 minutes to wilt it. Stir everything together, cover again and cook, stirring once or twice, until the potatoes are tender when pierced and the cabbage is soft and sweet, 10 to 12 minutes more. If the pan goes dry, add a few tablespoons of water.

Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high and cook 2 to 3 minutes so any extra liquid bubbles away and a few potatoes brown against the pan. Stir in the vinegar and mustard, season with pepper and more salt to taste, and scatter the dill over the top.

title: One-Pot Lemony Orzo with White Beans, Spinach and Parmesan
description: Orzo toasted and simmered risotto-style in broth, then folded with cannellini beans, baby spinach, lemon and Parmesan. A creamy vegetarian dinner for six from one pot, around $2 a serving.
notes: Traditional Parmesan is made with animal rennet, so look for a vegetarian hard cheese if that matters at your table. For a vegan version, use olive oil instead of butter and 2 tablespoons nutritional yeast instead of Parmesan, which removes the milk allergen. Chickpeas or butter beans can replace the cannellini, and chopped kale works in place of spinach if you give it 4 extra minutes. To add meat, stir in shredded leftover cooked chicken with the beans and heat until it reaches 165°F. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat covered with a few tablespoons of water until steaming and 165°F. Freezing makes the orzo soft, so it is better eaten within the week.

ingredients.name: cannellini beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

instructions: Warm the oil in a 5-quart Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of the salt and cook, stirring, until soft and translucent, 5 to 6 minutes. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute without letting the garlic brown.
Add the orzo and stir constantly until about half the pieces turn light golden and smell toasty, 2 to 3 minutes.

Pour in the broth and water, add the remaining salt and the oregano, and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to a steady simmer and cook uncovered, stirring every minute or two and scraping the bottom so nothing sticks, until the orzo is just tender and the liquid has turned creamy, 10 to 12 minutes.
Stir in the beans and cook 2 minutes to heat them through. Add the spinach a handful at a time, stirring until each addition wilts, about 2 minutes total.

Take the pot off the heat. Stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, Parmesan and butter until glossy. The orzo thickens as it stands, so loosen it with a splash of hot water if it turns stiff. Season with pepper, taste for salt and lemon, and top with the parsley.

title: Sheet-Pan Gochujang Chicken Thighs with Broccoli and Scallions
description: Boneless thighs coated in a sweet, spicy gochujang glaze and roasted hot on one pan beside broccoli until the edges char. A Korean-inspired dinner for four in about 40 minutes.
notes: Gochujang brands vary in heat; start with 2 tablespoons if you are feeding children. Most gochujang contains wheat, as does regular soy sauce, so this is not gluten-free unless you find a gluten-free gochujang and use gluten-free tamari. Serve with rice cooked ahead or reheated from the freezer, or wrap the chicken in crisp lettuce leaves. Cauliflower or green beans can replace the broccoli. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat in a 375°F oven or covered in the microwave until the chicken is 165°F. The cooked chicken freezes for up to 2 months, though the broccoli is better fresh.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs (about 6), trimmed and halved
broccoli florets (from 2 medium heads), cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
scallions, whites cut into 1-inch pieces, greens thinly sliced

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper-middle position. Line a rimmed half-sheet pan with parchment paper; the glaze is sticky and the paper saves scrubbing.

In a large bowl, whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, garlic, ginger and 1 tablespoon of the oil into a smooth paste. Add the chicken and turn to coat every piece. Let it sit while you prepare the broccoli, or cover and refrigerate up to 8 hours.

Toss the broccoli and the scallion whites on the pan with the remaining 2 tablespoons oil and the salt. Push the vegetables toward the edges and lay the chicken in the center in a single layer, smooth side up, scraping any glaze left in the bowl over it.

Roast until the chicken is browned at the edges and reads 165°F in the thickest piece and the broccoli is tender with charred tips, 20 to 25 minutes. Thighs stay juicy well past 165°F, so a few extra minutes for color is fine.

For deeper color, switch to the broiler for the last 2 minutes, watching closely because the honey burns quickly. Scatter the scallion greens over the pan and serve, spooning the pan juices over the chicken.

title: Sheet-Pan Sweet Chili Tofu with Sweet Potatoes and Green Beans
description: Cornstarch-dusted tofu roasts crisp beside sweet potatoes and green beans, then gets a sticky sweet chili, lime and tamari glaze. A vegan, peanut-free sheet-pan dinner for four, about $2 a serving.
notes: Press the tofu well: dry tofu crisps, wet tofu steams. The sauce has no peanuts or tree nuts, but check the sweet chili sauce label for your household, and for gluten if that matters. Low-sodium soy sauce can replace the tamari, which adds wheat. Broccoli florets, bell pepper strips or carrot coins can stand in for the green beans. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; the tofu softens in the fridge, so reheat on a sheet pan at 400°F for 8 to 10 minutes, until hot through (165°F), to bring back some crispness. Freezing is not recommended because the tofu turns spongy.

ingredients.name: sweet potato (1 large), scrubbed and cut into 3/4-inch cubes

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the center and line a rimmed half-sheet pan with parchment. Wrap the tofu in a clean kitchen towel and press it under a couple of heavy cans for 10 minutes while the oven heats.
Toss the sweet potato cubes on the pan with 1 tablespoon of the oil and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and spread them out. Roast for 10 minutes to give them a head start.

Meanwhile, cut the tofu into 3/4-inch cubes and put them in a large bowl. Toss gently with 1 tablespoon oil and 1/4 teaspoon salt, then sprinkle with the cornstarch and toss until no dry white patches remain.

Take the pan out, stir the sweet potatoes, and add the tofu in a single layer. Roast 15 minutes. While it roasts, toss the green beans in the same bowl with the last tablespoon of oil and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Add the green beans to the pan and flip the tofu. Roast until the tofu is golden and crisp at the edges, the sweet potatoes are browned and tender, and the beans are blistered, 10 to 12 minutes more.

Whisk the sweet chili sauce, tamari, lime juice, garlic and ginger in the bowl. Pour the sauce over the hot pan, toss everything with a spatula, and roast 2 minutes more so the glaze turns sticky. Top with the scallions and cilantro and serve with lime wedges.

title: Mexican-Style Chicken Fajita Bake with Black Beans and Corn Tortillas
description: Chicken, peppers and onion roasted on one sheet pan with fajita spices, plus a can of black beans so 1 1/2 pounds of chicken feeds six. The tortillas warm in the same oven; about $2.25 a serving.
notes: Boneless chicken breast works too; cut it the same size and start checking for 165°F at 20 minutes, since it dries out faster than thigh. To make it vegetarian, skip the chicken, double the black beans and add a sliced zucchini. Sour cream or shredded cheese on top is good and adds milk. Leftovers make quick burrito bowls or quesadilla fillings. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; reheat on a sheet pan at 400°F or covered in a skillet until the chicken is 165°F. The cooked filling freezes up to 2 months.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1/2-inch strips
bell peppers (any color), cut into 1/2-inch strips
large yellow onion, halved and sliced 1/2 inch thick
black beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
tomato salsa or pico de gallo

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with racks in the center and upper-middle positions. Line a rimmed half-sheet pan with foil for easy cleanup.

In a large bowl, stir together the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, oregano and salt. Add the chicken, peppers, onion and oil and toss until everything is evenly coated with spice. Wash your hands well after handling the raw chicken.
Spread the mixture on the pan in an even layer, keeping the chicken mostly on top of the vegetables and around the edges, where it browns best. Roast on the center rack for 15 minutes.

Stir, then scatter the black beans over the pan. Wrap the tortillas in foil in two stacks and set the packets on the upper rack. Roast until the chicken is browned at the edges and reads 165°F and the peppers are soft and charred in spots, 10 to 15 minutes more.

Squeeze the lime juice over the pan and toss. Set the pan on the table and let everyone fill warm tortillas with chicken, peppers and beans, topped with salsa, avocado, cilantro and a squeeze from the lime wedges.

title: Sheet-Pan Cauliflower and Chickpea Curry with Basmati Rice
description: Curry-spiced cauliflower, chickpeas and onion roast on one pan until browned, then bake in a quick coconut milk, tomato and ginger sauce. Served over basmati rice, it is a vegan dinner for four at about $2.50 a serving.
notes: Mild curry powder keeps this gentle enough for children; add the cayenne or the sliced chile for heat at the table. Coconut milk is not dairy, so the dish stays vegan; a spoonful of plain whole-milk yogurt on top is good but adds milk and makes it vegetarian rather than vegan. Stir 1 cup frozen peas into the sauce before it goes on the pan, or swap a cubed sweet potato for a third of the cauliflower. Refrigerate the curry and rice within 2 hours, spreading the rice out so it cools quickly, and keep both up to 4 days. Reheat covered with a splash of water until steaming and 165°F. The curry freezes up to 3 months; freeze the rice separately.

ingredients.name: basmati rice (280 g), rinsed until the water runs clear
head cauliflower (about 2 lb), cut into 1 1/2-inch florets
chickpeas (15 oz each), drained, rinsed and patted dry
large yellow onion, cut into 1-inch wedges
full-fat coconut milk (13.5 oz), well shaken
serrano or green chile, thinly sliced

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper-middle position. Put the rice, the 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook 15 minutes, then take the pan off the heat and leave it covered for at least 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, toss the cauliflower, chickpeas and onion with the coconut oil, curry powder, garam masala, cumin, cayenne if using, and 1/2 teaspoon salt until evenly yellow. Spread on a rimmed half-sheet pan in a single layer.
Roast, stirring once halfway, until the cauliflower is browned at the edges and just tender when pierced and the chickpeas are starting to crisp, about 25 minutes.

While the vegetables roast, set aside 1/4 cup of the coconut milk for serving. In the same bowl, whisk the rest of the coconut milk with the tomato paste, garlic, ginger and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt until smooth.
Pour the sauce over the pan and stir with a spatula to coat everything. Roast until the sauce bubbles, thickens and clings to the vegetables and the cauliflower is fully tender, 8 to 10 minutes.

Stir the lime juice into the curry and taste for salt. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve the curry over it, drizzled with the reserved coconut milk and topped with cilantro, sliced chile if you like, and lime wedges.

title: Sheet-Pan Ratatouille-Style Vegetables with Cannellini Beans
description: Eggplant, zucchini, pepper, onion and tomatoes roasted hot on one pan until jammy, then tossed with cannellini beans, garlic and vinegar. A Provençal-inspired vegan dinner for four at about $2.40 a serving.
notes: Serve with crusty bread, or with a fried egg on top for a vegetarian rather than vegan meal; the bread adds wheat and the egg adds eggs. Eggplant should be fully soft, not spongy, so give it the full time even if the zucchini looks done. Chickpeas or butter beans work in place of the cannellini. A spoonful of grated Parmesan on each plate is good and adds milk. It tastes even better the next day: refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 5 days, and eat it at room temperature or reheated until steaming and 165°F. It freezes for up to 3 months, though the zucchini softens; frozen portions make a good pasta sauce.

ingredients.name: medium eggplant (about 1 lb), cut into 1-inch cubes
zucchini (about 1 lb), halved lengthwise and cut into 3/4-inch half-moons
red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
ripe mixed tomatoes, cut into 1-inch wedges
cannellini beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper-middle position. In a large bowl, toss the eggplant with 2 tablespoons of the oil and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt first, since it soaks up oil quickly and needs its share.

Add the zucchini, bell pepper, onion, tomatoes, thyme, oregano, the remaining 2 tablespoons oil and 1/2 teaspoon salt, and toss again. Spread on a rimmed half-sheet pan; it will be full, which is fine, because the vegetables shrink as they roast.

Roast 25 minutes, then stir with a metal spatula, scraping up anything stuck to the pan, and scatter the garlic over the top. Roast until the eggplant is soft and creamy all the way through, the zucchini is browned at the edges and the tomatoes have collapsed into a jammy sauce, 15 to 20 minutes more.
Stir in the beans, red pepper flakes and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and roast 5 minutes, just until the beans are hot.
Drizzle with the vinegar, season with black pepper, and stir gently so the beans pick up the tomato juices. Taste for salt, scatter the basil over the top, and serve warm or at room temperature.
